„Hoffentlich bist du der Einzige in der Klasse, der so denkt!“
„Oh nein! Wir sind schon zu viert!“
Zu viert? Schon?
Und seit wann? „Erinnern Sie sich, Herr Lehrer, wie Sie damals die Sache über die Neger gesagt haben, noch im Frühjahr vor unserem Zeltlager? Damals haben wir doch alle unterschrieben, dass wir Sie nicht mehr haben wollen – aber ich tats nur unter Druck, denn Sie haben natürlich sehr recht gehabt mit den Negern. Und dann allmählich fand ich noch drei, die auch so dachten.“
units.en: “I hope you're the only one in the class who thinks like that!” “Oh no! There are four of us already!” Four? Already? And since when? “Do you remember, sir, when you said that thing about the Negroes, back in the spring before our camp? Back then we all signed that we didn't want you any more – but I only did it under pressure, because of course you were quite right about the Negroes. And then gradually I found three others who thought the same.”
units.explain_en: There is hope: not all young people are ‘fish’. ‘zu viert’ = four of us (zu zweit, zu dritt …) – very useful. ‘sich erinnern’ = to remember. ‘unter Druck’ = under pressure. ‘recht haben’ = to be right. ‘Ich tats’ = ‘Ich tat es’. ‘allmählich’ = gradually. Remember: ‘Neger’ is a racist slur today; say ‘Schwarze Menschen’.

units.en: The four boys, now joined by a baker's apprentice and an errand boy, have founded a secret club. Once a week they read everything that is banned. Mocking is strictly forbidden by their rules; instead they discuss how the world ought to be. The teacher remembers Z's words in court – that he only ever said how the world should be – and thinks of T, who only wants to know how things really are, so that he can sneer at them.

That's why I've come to you with my suspicion, to talk over with you what should be done.” “Why me, of all people?” “We all said it yesterday at the club, when we read in the paper about your evidence about the box: that you're the only adult we know who loves the truth.”

units.en: The investigating judge says the compass was stolen from the village mayor, probably by Eva's gang, so it no longer matters. The club decides to help Eva and to watch T day and night. B tells the teacher that his real nickname among the pupils isn't “the Fish” at all but “der Neger” – the racist word from his remark at the start – and they both laugh. The teacher's parents write, shocked that he has lost his job. He can't bring himself to write back “God will help”, until one evening he does, in the bar where Julius Caesar offers to help catch T. The club's daily reports say “nothing special”. Then the village priest visits, in ordinary clothes. Does the teacher realise he will never teach in this country again? And what will he live on?

„Ja, aber in einem anderen Land.“
„Wo?“

„Bei den Negern?“ Es fällt mir ein, dass ich „der Neger“ heiße, und ich muss lachen.

units.en: And I say: “I have nothing. And I have to support my parents too.” He looks at me wide-eyed and then, after a short pause, says: “I might have a position for you.” “What?! A position?!” “Yes, but in another country.” “Where?” “In Africa.” “With the Negroes?” It occurs to me that my nickname is “the Negro”, and I have to laugh. He remains serious. “Why do you find that so funny? Negroes are human beings too!”
units.explain_en: Nice irony: the priest repeats almost exactly the sentence that got the teacher into trouble at the start (‘Auch die Neger sind Menschen’). ‘unterstützen’ = to support. ‘die Stellung’ = position, job (today: ‘die Stelle’). ‘Es fällt mir ein’ = it occurs to me. ‘ernst bleiben’ = to stay serious. Again: ‘Neger’ is a racist slur today – say ‘Schwarze Menschen’.

Wem erzählen Sie das? möchte ich ihn fragen, aber ich sage nichts dergleichen, sondern höre es mir an, was er mir vorschlägt: ich könnte Lehrer werden, und zwar in einer Missionsschule.
„Ich soll in einen Orden eintreten?“
„Das ist nicht notwendig.“
Ich überlege. Heute glaube ich an Gott, aber ich glaube nicht daran, dass die Weißen die Neger beglücken, denn sie bringen ihnen Gott als schmutziges Geschäft.
Und ich sage es ihm.
Er bleibt ganz ruhig.
„Das hängt lediglich von Ihnen ab, ob Sie Ihre Sendung missbrauchen, um schmutzige Geschäfte machen zu können.“
Ich horche auf. Sendung?
„Jeder Mensch hat eine Sendung“, sagt er.
Richtig!
units.en: Who are you telling? I'd like to ask him, but I say nothing of the kind; instead I listen to what he proposes: I could become a teacher, at a mission school. “Am I supposed to join a religious order?” “That's not necessary.” I think it over. Today I believe in God, but I don't believe that the whites make the Negroes happy, because they bring them God as a dirty business. And I tell him so. He stays completely calm. “It depends entirely on you whether you misuse your mission to do dirty business.” I prick up my ears. Mission? “Every person has a mission,” he says. Right!
units.explain_en: ‘Wem erzählen Sie das?’ = Who are you telling? (I know that already!). ‘vorschlagen’ = to suggest. ‘in einen Orden eintreten’ = to join a religious order. ‘beglücken’ = to make happy (often ironic). The teacher criticises colonial missionaries. ‘abhängen von’ = to depend on – very useful. ‘missbrauchen’ = to misuse. ‘die Sendung’ here = mission, calling; today it usually means ‘TV programme’ or ‘parcel’! ‘Neger’ is a racist slur today.

units.en: The teacher says he will go to Africa once he has freed Eva. The priest advises him to tell T's mother everything. The teacher rides out to a grand villa, but the rich mother has no time for him; T appears instead, looking empty and frightened. Julius Caesar tries to trap T with the help of two women he knows from a nightclub, but T never turns up. That night the teacher cannot sleep: he imagines dead N accusing him of sharing the guilt. In the middle of the night the police take him to T's villa. T has taken his own life. On his mother's dressing table was a note: “The teacher drove me to my death.” The mother screams that the teacher is to blame. The teacher explains what kind of boy T was. The mother has a fit and drops a crumpled scrap of paper.

Der Funktionär hebt es auf.
Es ist ein zerknülltes Papier.
Der abgerissene Teil jenes Zettels, auf dem stand: „Der Lehrer trieb mich in den Tod“.
Und hier schrieb der T, warum er in den Tod getrieben wurde: „Denn der Lehrer weiß es, dass ich den N erschlagen habe. Mit dem Stein –“
Es wurde sehr still im Saal.
Die Mutter schien zusammengebrochen.
Sie saß und rührte sich nicht.
Plötzlich lächelt sie wieder und nickt mir zu.
units.en: The official picks it up. It is a crumpled piece of paper. The torn-off part of that note which said: “The teacher drove me to my death.” And here T had written why he was driven to his death: “Because the teacher knows that I killed N. With the stone –” It became very quiet in the hall. The mother seemed to have collapsed. She sat there and did not move. Suddenly she smiles again and nods to me.
units.explain_en: The truth comes out: T was the murderer, and his mother had torn off the second half of his note. ‘der Funktionär’ = official (here a senior police officer). ‘abreißen’ = to tear off. ‘der Zettel’ = note, slip of paper – very common. ‘in den Tod treiben’ = to drive to one's death. ‘zusammenbrechen’ = to collapse. ‘nicken’ = to nod.

Was war das?
Nein, das war doch nicht sie –
Das waren nicht ihre Augen –
Still wie die dunklen Seen in den Wäldern meiner Heimat.
Und traurig wie eine Kindheit ohne Licht.
So schaut Gott zu uns herein, muss ich plötzlich denken. Einst dachte ich, er hätte tückische, stechende Augen – Nein, nein!
Denn Gott ist die Wahrheit.
„Sage es, dass du das Kästchen erbrochen hast“, höre ich wieder die Stimme. „Tu mir den Gefallen und kränke mich nicht –“
units.en: What was that? No, that wasn't her – Those weren't her eyes – Still, like the dark lakes in the forests of my homeland. And sad, like a childhood without light. That is how God looks in at us, I suddenly think. Once I thought He had spiteful, piercing eyes – No, no! For God is truth. “Say that you broke open the box,” I hear the voice again. “Do me this favour and do not hurt me –”
units.explain_en: These are ‘die anderen Augen’ (the other eyes) of the chapter title: the same words described Eva's eyes in court. Now the teacher believes God looked at him through them. ‘tückisch’ = spiteful, treacherous. ‘stechend’ = piercing. ‘einst’ = once, in the past (formal). ‘Denn Gott ist die Wahrheit’ sums up his new faith: God is truth.

units.en: T's mother steps forward and admits, quietly but firmly, that she tore off the second half of the note. She wanted to spare the family the disgrace, she says, but when the teacher spoke about the children in the windows, she knew there was no point in hiding it any more. In the last chapter, “Über den Wassern” (Over the Waters), the teacher gets ready to leave.

units.de: Morgen fahre ich nach Afrika. Auf meinem Tische stehen Blumen. Sie sind von meiner braven Hausfrau zum Abschied. Meine Eltern haben mir geschrieben, sie sind froh, dass ich eine Stellung habe und traurig, dass ich so weit weg muss über das große Meer.
units.en: Tomorrow I leave for Africa. There are flowers on my table. They are from my good landlady, as a goodbye. My parents have written to me; they are glad that I have a job and sad that I have to go so far away, across the great sea.
units.explain_en: The ending mirrors the very first page: flowers from the landlady on his table and a letter from his parents. ‘zum Abschied’ = as a farewell (der Abschied = goodbye). ‘die Stellung’ = job (today: ‘die Stelle’). ‘froh’ and ‘traurig’ together – mixed feelings. ‘weit weg’ = far away.

units.de: Und dann ist noch ein Brief da. Ein blaues Kuvert. „Schöne Grüße an die Neger. Der Klub.“ Gestern hab ich Eva besucht. Sie ist glücklich, dass der Fisch gefangen wurde. Der Pfarrer hat es mir versprochen, dass er sich um sie kümmern wird, wenn sie das Gefängnis verlässt. Ja, sie hat Diebsaugen. Die Staatsanwaltschaft hat das Verfahren gegen mich niedergeschlagen, und der Z ist schon frei. Ich packe meine Koffer. Julius Caesar hat mir seinen Totenkopf geschenkt. Dass ich ihn nur nicht verliere! Pack alles ein, vergiss nichts! Lass nur nichts da! Der Neger fährt zu den Negern.
units.en: And there's another letter. A blue envelope. “Best wishes to the Negroes. The Club.” Yesterday I visited Eva. She is happy that the Fish has been caught. The priest has promised me that he will look after her when she leaves prison. Yes, she has thief's eyes. The public prosecutor has dropped the case against me, and Z is already free. I pack my suitcases. Julius Caesar has given me his skull. I mustn't lose it! Pack everything, don't forget anything! Don't leave anything behind! The Negro is going to the Negroes.
units.explain_en: The last line is bitterly ironic: his nickname and the slur from the first chapter come back – ‘Neger’ is a racist word; today say ‘Schwarze Menschen’. ‘Schöne Grüße an …’ = best wishes to … – very common. ‘sich kümmern um’ = to look after. ‘das Verfahren niederschlagen’ = to drop the case (today: ‘einstellen’). ‘Dass ich ihn nur nicht verliere!’ = I must make sure I don't lose it. ‘Lass nichts da!’ = don't leave anything here.
